Encore 0.2.0 adds your listening history, playlist management and a Song /
Video switch.

## Download

| System | File |
|---|---|
| macOS (Apple silicon and Intel) | `Encore_0.2.0_universal.dmg` |
| Windows 10 and 11 | `Encore_0.2.0_x64-setup.exe` (or the `.msi`) |
| Debian, Ubuntu | `Encore_0.2.0_amd64.deb` |
| Other Linux | `Encore_0.2.0_amd64.AppImage` |

Playback needs **Python 3.10+** and **Node.js, Deno or Bun** installed. See
[Install](https://github.com/Nayhap/encore#install) for one-line commands.

## First launch

These builds are not code-signed yet.

- **macOS:** open the app once, then go to **System Settings → Privacy &
  Security** and choose **Open Anyway**. macOS asks once for access to your
  saved session in the Keychain.
- **Windows:** SmartScreen warns on first run. Choose **More info**, then
  **Run anyway**. If Smart App Control is on, Windows blocks the app.

## What's new

- Songs you play in Encore show up in your YouTube Music history and shape
  your recommendations, as in the official app. Turn this off in Settings →
  Playback.
- A History page in the sidebar shows what you played, grouped by day, with
  "Remove from history"
- Create, rename and delete playlists, change their description, and make
  them private, unlisted or public
- Reorder your playlists by dragging, or with Move up and Move down
- "Add to playlist" can start a new playlist, and asks before adding a song
  that's already there
- Switch between a song and its music video from the now playing panel or
  any track's menu. The video plays as audio only.

Encore is unofficial and not affiliated with YouTube or Google.
